description: An OIDC identity presented by a P-256 sender (`aid:pubkey:p256:`, kat-keypair-005-p256) MUST verify. The JWT's `cnf.jkt` is the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the EC JWK `{"crv":"P-256","kty":"EC","x":…,"y":…}` whose `x`/`y` are the coordinates of the decompressed SEC1 point in the AID (RFC-AITP-0002 §2.2.1, RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.4): `kat-jwk-thumb-005-p256`, `6uuEaX_87uMh4VKEtSDkENgjC0g7Evt6vliSnD7XSDE`. A verifier that builds the OKP Ed25519 JWK for every AID, or puts the 44-char compressed identifier in `x`, computes a different thumbprint and fails this fixture.

expected.rationale: Every RFC-AITP-0002 §2.3 step passes. `__VALID_JWT__` is minted with `aud` = `self_aid`, `nonce` = the payload `pop_nonce`, and `cnf.jkt` = the thumbprint of the sender AID's key in the algorithm form of that AID (PLACEHOLDERS.md). For this P-256 AID the canonical JWK is the 126-byte EC form of `kat-jwk-thumb-005-p256`, members in lexicographic order (`crv`, `kty`, `x`, `y`).

$comment: Issue #68. RFC-AITP-0002 §2.2.1 used to pin the `cnf.jkt` JWK to the Ed25519 OKP form "exactly", so an OIDC-bound agent with a P-256 AID had no conformant `cnf.jkt` although P-256 AIDs are mandatory to verify in v0.2. This fixture pins the EC case. The envelope, Manifest and PoP signatures are P-256 (`agentP256` role); the OIDC issuer key is the runner's test issuer, as in every other `__VALID_JWT__` fixture.
